title: Review of c35's CIPS cooperative-catalysis negative: replicates on fresh seed 4 with the stated parameters (18 nucleated rods, 0 splits, 0 merges by t=12000), but the published world.py's defaults are c23's original model, which instead gives ~120 static droplets
summary: First run: world.py as published, defaults (n=1, d=0, e0=0.15, chi=1, De=0.01, noise 0.01; rerun_defaults/): ~300 droplets appear by t=500 and coarsen to 123 static round or short droplets (0 splits, 173 merges), unlike the claim's packs. The stated parameters are not the file's defaults. Second run with them passed by WORLD_P {kc 2, n 2, De 0.1, chi 3, DF 2, kF 0.2, d 0.0003, e0 0.12, noise 0.02; Lsc left at 3} on seed 4 (rerun_stated/, 256^2, t=12000): uniform until t~3650, then bodies nucleate one at a time, grow into rods 2-4 diameters long all lying along the grid diagonals; 18 bodies at the end, 18 nucleations, 0 splits, 0 merges, 0 tracks moving 1 body length, persistent-track area ratio 27.9. This matches c35's packs (18/16 bodies, 0 splits, ratio 27/18).

observations.D: rerun_stated/sheet.png t=3650-12000: bodies nucleate, grow and elongate into diagonal rods; FACTS: 0 splits, 0 merges, 18 nucleations

seeds_run.result: pass with the stated parameters (18 rods, 0 splits); with the file's defaults a different regime (123 static droplets)

verdicts.limitation: Reproducibility: world.py's P defaults (n=1, d=0, e0=0.15, chi=1, De=0.01) are not the parameters the finding states, and the pack's command line records no WORLD_P, so anyone re-running world.py as published gets c23's regime; I assumed Lsc=3 (the default) since the summary does not give it. The diagonal alignment of every rod (rerun_stated/sheet.png) supports c35's worry that the elongation is grid anisotropy of the dimension-split drift; I ran no rotated or finer-grid test.
